objective: Make Jamie immediately legible as a Technical Project Manager - Product Operations & Implementation lead while preserving factual support, collective credit, consent, accessibility, and exact-commit release discipline.

hardGates.description: Citation, type, lint, build, knowledge-bank, public-safety, route, and launch-eval checks pass.
Staging builds with staging canonicals and fail-closed noindex behavior.
The current production dependency audit has no high or critical advisories; lower-severity residual risks are explicitly reviewed and documented.
Production builds only with the explicit production URL and index policy.
Canonical routes have one H1, no horizontal overflow, and no console errors at every required viewport.
Keyboard focus, skip navigation, citations, headings, and primary actions remain semantically usable.
Jamie approves the exact staging-reviewed SHA that is promoted; no nearby branch or rebuilt variant may substitute for it.
Apex and www routing, TLS, health, canonicals, Open Graph, resume delivery, robots, and sitemap are verified after deployment.

judgeCriteria.label: Role legibility
judgeCriteria.intent: Within one viewport and three minutes, a hiring reader can name Jamie's target role, operating contribution, and relevant proof path.

anchors.1: The role is vague or requires reconstructing Jamie's identity from many projects.
anchors.3: The role is stated, but the connection between claims and proof requires effort.
anchors.5: The role, operating contribution, and next proof step are immediate, specific, and memorable.

judgeCriteria.label: Evidence and epistemic care
judgeCriteria.intent: Claims are concrete, source-backed where verification matters, bounded by what evidence establishes, and free of inflation.

anchors.1: Important claims are unsupported, overstated, or contradicted by their evidence.
anchors.3: Most claims are careful, but support or limitations are unevenly visible.
anchors.5: Every consequential claim is appropriately supported, qualified, and easy to inspect without exposing protected evidence.

judgeCriteria.label: Emerging-work framing
judgeCriteria.intent: The portfolio presents transition and under-formed structure without shaming teams, while remaining concrete enough for hiring readers.

anchors.1: The language blames, diagnoses, or romanticizes the people seeking help.
anchors.3: The language is humane but occasionally abstract or euphemistic.
anchors.5: The language makes emerging structure feel normal, actionable, and professionally precise.

judgeCriteria.label: Reader burden and hierarchy
judgeCriteria.intent: A time-limited reader can choose a clear path, scan the evidence, and act without carrying the archive's complexity.

anchors.1: The reader must explore broadly or decode internal language before understanding relevance.
anchors.3: The main path is visible, with some avoidable repetition or density.
anchors.5: Each surface advances one clear argument and the next action is obvious.

judgeCriteria.label: Chad lens
judgeCriteria.intent: A hiring reader sees Jamie as the actor, understands what his work made usable and why it fits the target role, without carrying specialized archival or governance complexity; collective credit and evidence boundaries remain intact.

anchors.1: The archive, project, or values dominate; Jamie's action and hiring relevance must be reconstructed.
anchors.3: Jamie and the usable result are visible, but repeated metadata, specialized language, or governance detail interrupts the hiring argument.
anchors.5: Every key surface quickly states Jamie's action, usable result, and role relevance; secondary evidence and governance remain inspectable without interrupting the path, and collective credit stays precise.

judgeCriteria.label: Collective credit and protected boundaries
judgeCriteria.intent: Jamie's contribution is visible without appropriating collective outcomes or exposing people and records that should remain protected.

anchors.1: The page implies sole ownership, exposes protected material, or obscures collaborators' agency.
anchors.3: Collective language is mostly careful but Jamie's role or the boundary is occasionally unclear.
anchors.5: Jamie's contribution, collective context, and protected absences are all precise and mutually reinforcing.

judgeCriteria.label: Visual proof and credibility
judgeCriteria.intent: The visual system and approved evidence help readers inspect real work rather than merely accept descriptive copy.

anchors.1: Presentation is generic, broken, or substitutes decoration for proof.
anchors.3: The system is coherent and some evidence is inspectable, but key cases remain text-heavy.
anchors.5: A small number of decisive, approved artifacts make the work tangible without clutter or consent risk.

judgeCriteria.label: Operational credibility
judgeCriteria.intent: The site demonstrates that Jamie can coordinate implementation, create durable operating structure, and leave work maintainable after launch.

anchors.1: The portfolio describes values without showing operational practice or outcomes.
anchors.3: Operational skills are named and partly evidenced, but examples remain generic.
anchors.5: Requirements, workflows, decisions, launch support, adoption, and handoffs are connected to specific outcomes across contexts.

objectiveOrder: raise every judge criterion to its minimum
raise the weighted score to the target
reduce reader effort without weakening evidence or boundaries
iteration: Record the starting commit and run every hard gate.
Render all runtime cases and collect only public-safe evidence.
Ask a fresh judge context to score every criterion with cited page evidence.
Choose the lowest-scoring criterion and state one falsifiable improvement hypothesis.
Make the smallest coherent change that tests that hypothesis.
Re-run all hard gates and the affected runtime cases, then re-score the full rubric.
Keep the change only if no hard gate fails, no criterion regresses beyond the allowed maximum, and the objective improves.
Commit the accepted iteration with its eval report; otherwise revert only that iteration.
antiGaming: Never improve a score by deleting guardrails, qualifications, sources, collective credit, or protected boundaries.
Never improve the Chad lens by hiding Jamie's role, deleting unique evidence, or making publication boundaries unavailable.
Never expose private evidence to make a public claim easier to judge.
Never tune only one viewport, route, persona, or judge phrasing.
Never replace an approved resume, contact fact, or metric without Jamie's explicit review.
Never promote a different SHA from the one that passed staging review.
hillClimb.stopWhen: All hard gates pass and the weighted target plus every criterion minimum are met in two consecutive fresh-judge runs.
